title: Russia Strikes Kharkiv 9-Story Apartment Building on Ceasefire Day 2 — 8 Wounded Including 2 Children
detail: Less than 24 hours into the Trump-brokered 3-day ceasefire, Russia struck a 9-story residential building in Kharkiv's Industrial district with a drone. Kharkiv Gov. Oleh Syniehubov reported 8 civilians wounded, including 2 children. Two 8-year-old boys suffered acute stress reactions. The strike came despite Russia having confirmed participation in the May 9–11 ceasefire announced by President Trump. Ukraine's Air Force intercepted all 27 drones Russia launched overnight from Primorsko-Akhtarsk and Millerovo, but the Kharkiv attack used a drone that penetrated air defenses. Across Ukraine, Russia continued combat activity: Russian forces launched ground assaults in the Pokrovsk, Lyman, Kramatorsk, and Zaporizhzhia directions throughout May 10. A 67-year-old civilian was killed in Zaporizhzhia Oblast and a 46-year-old woman was killed in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast in separate Russian drone strikes during the declared ceasefire period.

title: Putin Claims War 'Coming to an End,' Offers to Meet Zelenskyy — But Only After Peace Treaty Finalized
detail: On May 10, a day into the Trump-brokered ceasefire, Russian President Vladimir Putin declared that Russia's war on Ukraine is 'coming to an end' and offered to meet President Zelenskyy in a neutral third country — but only after a peace treaty is finalized, not during active negotiations. The Kremlin simultaneously said it expects US envoys to arrive 'quite soon' but conditioned further talks on Ukrainian withdrawal from parts of Donetsk — a demand Ukraine has firmly rejected. Putin made these statements while Russia continued to violate the declared ceasefire with ground assaults and drone strikes. Zelenskyy responded that Ukraine would 'strictly mirror' Russian actions, adding that Russia began May 10 with shelling and assault operations. Trump told reporters he was hopeful: 'I'd like to see a big extension. It could be.' The gap between Russia's stated diplomatic openness and its continued kinetic activity underscored Western skepticism about Moscow's ceasefire intentions.

media.caption: Putin claims war is 'coming to an end' as ceasefire holds partially on Day 2 — May 10, 2026

title: Ceasefire Day 2: 121+ Combat Clashes, 1 Killed, 19 Injured Across Ukraine — Trump Hopes for Extension
detail: On May 10, the second day of the Trump-brokered 3-day ceasefire (May 9–11), Ukraine reported 121–150 combat clashes and continued Russian drone and missile activity despite the declared truce. Russia and Ukraine traded mutual accusations of violations: Russia claimed Ukraine committed over 1,000 violations; Ukraine documented continued Russian ground assaults in all main frontline directions — Pokrovsk, Lyman, Kramatorsk, Zaporizhzhia, and Kherson. At least 1 civilian was killed (67-year-old, Zaporizhzhia Oblast) and 19+ injured across Ukraine during the ceasefire period on May 10. Ukraine's Air Force intercepted all 27 drones Russia launched overnight from Primorsko-Akhtarsk and Millerovo bases. Russian cumulative personnel losses since February 24, 2022 reached 1,341,110 per the Ukrainian General Staff's May 10 report. US President Trump expressed continued optimism: 'I'd like to see a big extension. It could be.' President Zelenskyy's office said Ukraine 'strictly mirrors' Russian actions and would continue defending frontline positions. A separate update: Hungary's new government signaled an end to its EU aid veto, potentially unlocking the €90 billion loan package to Kyiv that had been stalled.

media.caption: Ukraine and Russia exchange ceasefire violation accusations on Day 2 as Trump hopes for extension — May 10, 2026
